title: Why Is Elbit Systems Ltd. (ESLT) Stock Up +7.30% Today?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
# Key Takeaways

* Elbit Systems Ltd. ([ESLT](https://tickeron.com/ticker/ESLT/)) is up 7.30%, or $49.71, at $730.45 in early trading, after closing the prior session at $680.74.
* The primary catalyst is a third-quarter earnings beat: revenue rose 17% to $2.25 billion and adjusted EPS of $4.36 came in above consensus.
* Secondary drivers include a record $33 billion order backlog, a new 2027 outlook calling for high-teens revenue growth, and a $1.00 per-share dividend.
* The gain is company-specific. Defense shares broadly have been choppy as investors weigh the post-midterm outlook for U.S. defense spending.
* **News Significance Score: 60/100** — Solid earnings beat and record backlog; the price jump was about 3.8x the stock's typical daily move.
* Traders are watching the analyst call, backlog conversion timing, margin durability and the pace of European orders.

* Explore [Trending AI Robots](https://tickeron.com/bot-trading/trending-robots/) to see which automated strategies are leading in current market conditions.

# Opening Summary

Elbit Systems Ltd. ([ESLT](https://tickeron.com/ticker/ESLT/)) is a Haifa-based defense technology company that builds unmanned aircraft, electro-optics, electronic warfare suites, command-and-control systems, precision munitions and high-power lasers for Israel and export customers across Europe, Asia-Pacific and North America. Shares jumped 7.30% to $730.45 in the first half-hour of Tuesday's session, up $49.71 from Monday's close of $680.74, reversing part of a sharp four-week slide. The move is directly attributable to third-quarter results published before the opening bell, which beat on revenue and adjusted profit and lifted the order backlog to a record.

# Earnings Beat and a Record $33 Billion Backlog

Revenue rose 17% to $2.252 billion from $1.922 billion a year earlier, ahead of consensus near $2.16 billion. GAAP net income climbed to $177.9 million from $133.4 million, with diluted EPS of $3.70 versus $2.80; on an adjusted basis, EPS reached $4.36, comfortably above analyst estimates. Adjusted operating income rose to $244.1 million, or 10.8% of revenue, from 9.7% a year ago, and gross margin widened to 25.3%.

The headline number was the backlog: $33.0 billion at September 30, up from $25.2 billion a year earlier and a fresh record, with 74% of orders from outside Israel and Europe driving the quarterly increase. Growth was concentrated in Land and Armaments, up 28% to $758.7 million on Israeli ammunition demand, and ISTAR and Electronic Warfare, up 32% to $449.7 million on laser, maritime and electro-optic sales. Aerospace lagged at 4%.

# 2027 Guidance, Cash Flow and the Dividend

Management guided 2027 revenue growth in the high teens with continued margin expansion, an explicit extension of the growth story that investors had been questioning after a 28% drawdown from the 52-week high of $1,016.06. Free cash flow of $276 million in the quarter represented cash conversion above 150%, and nine-month operating cash flow nearly doubled to $862.5 million. The board declared a $1.00-per-share dividend payable January 4. Offsets included a higher effective tax rate of 11.6% and roughly $27 million of costs to terminate U.S. pension plans.

# Contract Momentum Across Europe and Israel

The quarter capped a run of awards that underpins the guidance: $260 million for PULS rocket artillery to a European NATO member, $235 million in launchers and EXTRA-MR rockets to another European customer, $200 million of Asia-Pacific airborne ISTAR work, $170 million for an IDF artillery training center, and about $270 million in ISR and targeting payloads. Elbit also said it signed an agreement with Israel's Ministry of Defense to be compensated for payment delays dating to October 2023 — a quiet but material cash-flow positive.

# Market Context and Trading Activity

The advance is not a sector-wide event. Defense shares have been uneven as investors digest U.S. budget politics, and Elbit's own tape had been weak: the stock fell 15.7% from its October 29 close of $807.41 to Monday's $680.74, with two consecutive sessions of roughly 7% declines in early November on heavy turnover. That left the shares oversold into the print, and the gap higher carries the signature of a relief rally layered on short covering.

Liquidity is modest — average daily volume runs near 87,000 shares on Nasdaq against a float of about 27.5 million shares — so a post-earnings repricing of this size is characteristic of the name. Technically, the stock has reclaimed the $700 level and is testing the $735–$740 zone that capped several sessions in recent weeks, with the $650 November low now the key downside reference. Market capitalization sits near $34 billion.

# News Significance Score

The score runs from 0 to 100, where 0 means no meaningful news and a move typical for the stock, and 100 means transformative news paired with an extreme, rare price move. Here the score is 60 out of 100. The verified news was substantial: a revenue beat, adjusted earnings ahead of consensus, a record $33 billion backlog and a newly framed high-teens outlook for 2027 — all material relative to a company of this size, though short of a step-change event. The price move was roughly 3.8 times the stock's average absolute daily change over the past 60 sessions, and only one session in that window produced a larger one-day swing. Strong news and a moderately rare move combine into a mid-range score.

# What Comes Next for ESLT

Attention now shifts to the 9:00 a.m. Eastern conference call, where analysts are likely to press on the slower conversion of backlog into revenue — about 35% is scheduled for performance through the end of 2027, down from 42% a quarter earlier — and on capacity expansion, supply chain execution and European demand visibility. Fourth-quarter results and the formal 2027 outlook arrive early next year, with the $1.00 dividend payable January 4. Risks include U.S. and European budget politics, restrictions on engagement with Israel in some markets, component and shipping costs tied to Red Sea disruptions, currency effects and a valuation that still embeds aggressive growth assumptions.
